LHX.sentence: L3Harris bounced more than 6% in a single day after a long slide — it's the smallest of the five big US defense contractors, and with military spending still rising, nothing about the underlying business has really changed.

ASML.sentence: ASML is quiet this week — once you account for next year's expected growth, the Dutch company that makes the world's only machines for printing the most advanced chips looks far less pricey than its headline numbers suggest.

LIN.sentence: Linde dipped slightly, but the story never changes: they supply oxygen, nitrogen and other industrial gases under long contracts and nudge prices up a little each quarter.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm this week — its Azure cloud business is still growing strongly as AI companies rent its computing power, so the big AI story keeps grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is steady, and early signs of biotech funding thawing are encouraging, since fresh money into labs tends to show up as more orders for its equipment a couple of quarters later.

CVX.sentence: Chevron ticked up a little, and its profits look fat right now mainly because fighting involving Iran has pushed oil well above normal — that's the oil price swelling the numbers, not the company itself suddenly doing better.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow plunged roughly 27% in a single day — a rare, dramatic drop — even though big companies and US government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI-assistant software under long-term contracts, so this looks more like panic than a broken business.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore was essentially flat, with its commodity-trading arm earning the market's respect even as copper prices sag, and it's paying out a hefty share of cash to shareholders along the way.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta jumped about 5%, and the key number — the price it gets for a ton of crushed stone — is still climbing, which is exactly the local-quarry advantage that makes this business tick.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA was quiet, though a weaker Mexican peso is a mild headwind since most of this Latin American Coke bottler's earnings are in pesos that convert to fewer dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber barely moved, and people keep booking more rides and food orders than ever — the real question hanging over it is whether self-driving car companies choose to put their cars on Uber's app or go it alone.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk was flat, and the market is pricing this Danish container-shipping giant below what it would even cost to rebuild its fleet of ships — a sign expectations for global trade are pretty gloomy right now.

MA.sentence: Mastercard rose more than 4% and is oddly trading a hair cheaper than its twin Visa, even though people keep tapping their cards more than ever and Mastercard collects a tiny toll on each swipe.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company had a steady day and is trading below its own recent norms, while hospitals keep performing more operations with its machines — and every surgery means more disposable supplies sold.
